label: Modal grounding frameworks at the foundational case and Pruss's Aristotelian-modality route
summary:
#1887 tests 4 and 5 (slice A), God-existence stage; note docs/notes/modal-grounding-frameworks.md; repaired after the independent semantic challenge of head 44f70bff. Analyst formulations, attribution deferred, navigation only. All accounts of de re possibility of absence are framework inputs on the shared CausalityFrame at one matching scope, the foundational case FoundationalAt (DEF 7fcf846e). Verdicts: PGP with excluded middle gives 'necessary' (1e6174ab; only actuality, incorruptibility and no-power are used); B6 with excluded middle gives 'necessary' (39df9612); unconditional essentialism (essence grounds necessity plus esse = essence read as existence in the nature, the ESSENCE_3 to ESSENCE_5 sense bridge; Essential registered as ESSENCE_5 of DISAMB-ESSENCE) supports B6 constructively (f9b26559); existence-conditional essentialism gives 'possibly absent' with esse = essence idle (872a3832); combinatorial: existing recombinationGivesContingency and law 2 (constructive); primitivist: the non-modal profile fixes neither verdict; hybrid: inherits its verdict from its existence component (possibly absent with a combinatorial component, none with a primitivist one), and its model shows consistency with the First Way premises only. The necessity verdict and a concrete foundational being give STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT (b27c88b0). Test 5: the first reconstruction (f90934ad, projection 2a3a3f09) uses the global possibility that no contingent concretum exists (0dc833c1), a stronger analyst variant that Pruss declines ('The Actual and the Possible', read by the semantic challenge); its Euclidean premise and omission 6 are artefacts of that variant. Pruss's own premise, that some accessible world lacks every actual contingent concretum with others perhaps in their stead (18e5bd4e), gives the necessary concrete power-holder b90ee2de without any Euclidean premise (42da6b2d; projection ad42c376 to the node; controls 6cf3a8ce: nonvacuity on theist and non-Euclidean frames, five omission models, replacement versus joint absence, the S4 conceivability bundle; law: on Euclidean frames the global premise implies Pruss's). Coordinator requests: F1 built (law 9, one-sided models, S4 bundle model); F2 built as the receptive/subjectless factorization replacing #1888's requested equivalence, without a registered strength_comparison relation or power disambiguation; F3 built (law 10); F4 covered by f9b26559, 872a3832, laws 3-4 and the conditional-essence model; F5 already exists (subtraction batch).

Curation pass 2, lane D (#2103, 2026-11-27). ef54f023 tests 20d5fecd. Omit power grounding of contingency at reading world true. In bruteFirst the foundational mover exists there and is absent at the other accessible world, despite being incorruptible simply and under no bearer’s power over its esse. Both power grounding and the necessity verdict fail. ef54f023 tests 96971e31. Omit the premise that beings contingent at the reading world have distinct esse and essence. In bruteFirst the foundational mover true is contingent at true and its represented esse and essence agree, so the foundational necessity verdict fails. ef54f023 tests 54bafc9f. Omit the principle that essential existence entails necessary existence. The bruteFirst profile assigns the mover's existence to its nature and satisfies the esse-to-essential-existence bridge. The mover is absent at an accessible world, and the distinct-esse verdict fails. ef54f023 tests 565ccd6c. Omit the bridge from equality of esse and essence to essential existence. On bruteFirst the essential predicate is empty. Essential truths entail necessity vacuously, while the contingent mover has equal esse and essence and the bridge fails. ef54f023 tests 94393b5b. Omit grounding for the global absence possibility. In creatureFrame at true there is a contingent concretum and an accessible world with no contingent concretum. No candidate has a power for the latter proposition. Initiator presence and holder concreteness hold vacuously. ef54f023 tests fffa0693. Omit initiator presence for the global absence possibility. In creatureFrame the sole power holder is the contingent creature false, which exists at the reading world true but is absent from the only accessible outcome with no contingent concretum. ef54f023 tests 2d2be120. Omit concreteness of the global-absence power holder. In theistFrame true holds the power and is present at the origin and at the outcome, while only the contingent bearer false is concrete. The other nonlogical premises hold and the concrete holder conclusion fails. ef54f023 tests 0dc833c1. Omit the possibility of a world without any world-local contingent concretum. In swappedFrame at true the present contingent bearer can be absent, but another contingent concretum is present at the replacement world. The global absence proposition fails everywhere. ef54f023 tests c76b6e2c. Omit the actual contingent-concretum premise in the global route. In emptyFrame the existence extension is empty at both worlds, including the reading world true. The absence proposition is accessible, and there is no existing power holder. ef54f023 tests 62b4a40a. Omit Euclidean access. In nonEuclidean at a, the power holder true is present at a and at the contingent-free accessible world b, which accesses only itself. That holder is absent at c, also accessible from a, so the required origin-relative necessity fails. ef54f023 retains a nonlogical witness for be4b04bf. The whole-argument link to be4b04bf from #2116 was removed. TheistModel does not certify ExcludedMiddle over arbitrary propositions. At true in theistFrame, false is a present contingent concretum, and the other accessible world has no contingent concretum. The power holder true is concrete and exists at both worlds. All global-route nonlogical premises hold in this model. ef54f023 tests 3847c481. At true in theistFrame, bearer true is a concrete foundational being and the foundational necessity condition holds. It witnesses the positive joint premise bundle on the same frame. ef54f023 tests 06327949. In theistFrame at true, essential existence of bearer true is assigned explicitly and it is present at every accessible world. The essentialist necessity law and the bridge from esse equal to essence hold jointly. 6cf3a8ce tests 95bf8780. Omit grounding for absence of the actual contingent roster. At true in creatureFrame the contingent creature exists and is absent at the other accessible world. No candidate has a power for its absence, so no necessary concrete holder exists. 6cf3a8ce tests 906f5c39. Omit initiator presence for absence of the actual contingent roster. At true in creatureFrame only the existing contingent creature false holds the power. It is absent at the sole accessible world realizing the relevant absence. 6cf3a8ce tests a6906cab. Omit concreteness of the actual-absence power holder. In theistFrame true alone holds that power and is present in the outcome world. The concrete predicate singles out false, which is contingent at the reading world true. 6cf3a8ce tests 18e5bd4e. Omit joint absence of those concreta that are contingent at the origin. In vanCleveFrame at (true, true), both origin-contingent candidates can individually be absent, but every accessible world has at least one of them. The remaining nonlogical premises hold with no powers assigned. 6cf3a8ce tests c76b6e2c. Omit the premise that some concretum is contingent at the origin. In emptyFrame no candidate exists at true or at its accessible world. Joint absence is accessible for the empty roster, yet no candidate can witness the holder conclusion. 6cf3a8ce retains a nonlogical witness for 259571ae. The whole-argument link to 259571ae from #2116 was removed. SiblingNonvacuity does not certify ExcludedMiddle over arbitrary propositions. In theistFrame at true the actual contingent roster contains false and the other accessible world lacks it. True exists at both worlds and holds the assigned absence power. All nonlogical premises of the actual-roster variant are jointly satisfied.

Curation pass 2, lane D (#2103, 2026-11-27). The existence-conditional omissions inside ef54f023 concern 857654fe, 9d8a8d2e, 38200db5 and d1af2b06. All four are off the root path, so those models carry no new tests links. The global and actual-roster omissions have their own exact targets.
blocker: No premise is established. Independence (test 5): neither Pruss route needs PGP or C2 (prussWithoutPGP; the sibling has no such premise), but neither is independent of the C2 crux's general theory: P1 and P1-prime are power-grounded modality applied to a joint absence; for the global variant, with P4, Euclidean access and the transfer bridge (warrant open), P1 yields PGP's power channel for concrete contingents and the necessity verdict at concrete foundational beings (laws 5-6). Common ground: the global P4 is accepted by the theist and by rivals accepting subtraction, and contested by Lowe-style views on which some contingent being necessarily exists; Pruss's P4-prime is far weaker (compatible with replacement), and no recorded rival view is shown to deny it, so the datum moves from the foundational being's disputed possible absence to a possibility the rivals have no recorded reason to reject, and the rivals answer by denying P1-prime. Pruss's P4-prime is not entailed by each actual contingent's possible absence (Van Cleve model). Initiator presence is close to Pruss's principle but existential, builds in accessibility, and is mirrored in direction; it is not b62a64ab plus correlation; it fails on a tensed reading for a self-annihilating holder. #1888 finds parity between existence-conditional essentialism and PGP at the foundational being. Next tests: (1) whether existence never belonging to an essence applies to an esse-essence identity (decides between laws 3-4 and f9b26559); (2) a tensed initiator-presence variant over the frame's IsAt; (3) the transfer bridge's warrant; (4) a registered strength comparison for PGP's two halves; (5) a bridge from the holder to firstness, f9208664 or c71c068c; (6) Pruss's own direction (a power in w1 for w0's actuality, with S5) and iterated powers; (7) whether a power to abstain is a power in Aristotelian modality's sense (q.104 a.3 ad 1).
